text:
The Wild come home 15-3-4 with an 11-game point streak, eight straight road wins and two of the league's hottest players, and the conversation in Minnesota is still about whether Quinn Hughes stays. The Star Tribune ran an opinion piece headlined "We love your game, Quinn Hughes. Now make up your mind," and Elliotte Friedman's update on his future made the rounds the same week. On the ice, Hughes has 16 points in his last ten and an 11-game point streak, though our numbers say that run leans on bounces more than chances. Kirill Kaprizov has his own 11-game streak (6 goals, 14 assists) and the league's goal lead at last count.

Tonight is also Brock Faber's first home game of the season. He returned from a skull fracture on Saturday in Boston, and NHL.com's headline said he "didn't miss a beat." Olli Maatta went on injured reserve Monday with an upper-body injury.

Here is the part that should temper the celebration: Minnesota's results are running well ahead of its chances. A +28 goal difference rests on +16.6 expected, and Jesper Wallstedt is doing much of the lifting, 17.9 goals saved above expected and 5-0-0 at .942 over his last five. That is elite goaltending, and goaltending is the least steady thing in hockey.

Nashville brings its own heater in Juuse Saros, .947 over his last five starts after a season last year that finished 10.2 goals below expected. The Predators' seven-game winning streak ended Saturday in San Jose, and they have been outchanced at five on five this season (47% of the expected goals). Steven Stamkos has 9 points in his last five games against Minnesota, and Jonathan Marchessault is off the out list and day-to-day. Daemon Hunt returns to St. Paul after 56 games as a Wild. Our numbers favor Minnesota on chances, 3.37 expected goals to 2.64, which already counts both goalies' form.
headline: Two hot goalies, and Quinn Hughes's question hangs over it
